messages:
alex: seeing a burst of gRPC streaming stalls on /rpc/stream between inference pods across nodes in us-west-2a/us-west-2b since the kernel update at ~09:05 UTC. Streams hang, CPU fine, sockets stuck in ESTABLISHED but no packets progressing.

maya: same. p50 latency for pod-to-pod jumped from 8ms -> 80ms and a lot of retransmits on node NICs. Not a GPU issue.

sanjay: can you paste tcpdump or dmesg? any fragmentation messages?

alex: tcpdump from node-a to node-b while reproducing:
```
15:35:10.123456 IP 10.48.3.12.43210 > 10.48.7.8.50051: Flags [P.], seq 12345:22345, ack 54321, win 65535, options [nop,nop,TS val 123456 ecr 654321], length 10000
15:35:10.123789 IP (frag 0) 10.48.3.12 > 10.48.7.8: IP fragment overlapping or missing (frag reassembly failed)
```
Not super-precise but kernel dmesg shows a bunch of: 
"NET: Received packet smaller than min IPv4 header length" and "fragmented packet dropped (MTU?)"

infra-bot: ALERT: node-a retransmit-rate > 15% for >5m, implicated pods: inference/model-server-*

den a: suspect MTU/overlay fragmentation + host GSO/TSO interactions. We recently enabled jumbo frames on some instance types but CNI (calico VXLAN) overhead wasn't accounted for, so effective path MTU differs across hops. GSO may be producing large skbs that get fragmented in the overlay and reassembly fails for UDP/TCP/gRPC streaming.

ryan: quick checks: `ip link show` (host MTU), `ip -d link show vxlan.calico` (overlay MTU), `ethtool -k eth0` (offloads), `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing` and `ss -tin | grep retrans` and `iptables -t mangle -A PREROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu` as mitigation.

maya: ran commands on node-b:
```
$ ip link show eth0
3: eth0: mtu 9000 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
$ ip link show vxlan.calico
vxlan.calico: mtu 1450 ...
$ ethtool -k eth0
features: gso: on tso: on gro: on lro: off
```
So host NIC MTU 9000, VXLAN 1450. That mismatch explains it.

alex: so some packets leave as large GSO skbs assuming 9000, overlay slices them and kernel reassembly fails?

sanjay: yes — GSO/TSO will hand big segments to overlay; if intermediate devices can't handle fragmentation (e.g., offload vs VXLAN handling bug) you get reassembly holes. Also some kernels have known bugs re: fragmented GRE/VXLAN + GRO/GSO.

dena: short-term mitigation: disable GSO/TOSO/GRO on the host NICs for affected nodes:
```
ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off
```
and enable TCP PMTUD probing: `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`. Also add MSS clamping in iptables to avoid giant segments.

ryan: I tested disabling offloads on node-b and reran the grpc streaming test — no stalls and retransmit rate dropped to <1% in 2m. That looks like a reliable mitigation.

ops: what's the deployment plan? we need to avoid broad perf regression (CPU/tx overhead) from disabling offloads everywhere.

alex: plan suggestion:
- emergency: apply iptables MSS clamp on all nodes in us-west-2 to stop new stalls (no restart needed).
- targeted: disable GSO/GRO/TSO on the 6 nodes showing issues and cordon/drain them in a maintenance window, validate with synthetic streaming tests.
- long-term: align CNI MTU across AZs. Either: set host MTU to 1450 for all nodes (preferred if we can't do jumbo reliably across path) OR reconfigure CNI to use host-gw mode / avoid VXLAN or enable path MTU-aware overlay.
- kernel: track upstream bug; file kernel/CNI bugs if reproducible.

dena: add to rollout checklist: check SR-IOV / ENA driver settings for instances with jumbo frames; make sure inner/outer MTU math includes VXLAN (50 bytes). Also verify that cloud networking (VPC ENIs) support 9000 across the AZs — we had one subnet with 1500-only.

maya: quick commands to test path MTU: `ping -M do -s <size> <peer>` to find largest non-fragmenting size and `iperf3 -M` to test.

infra-bot: Created incident: INC-2026 - gRPC streaming stalls due to MTU/offload mismatch. Assigned to: sanjay, dena.

ops: I'll schedule a 2-hour maintenance this afternoon to roll the affected nodes with the targeted offload disable and validation. Will notify customers and add fallback routing to Dedicated pools for high-traffic tenants.

alex: created a quick runbook in the ticket with commands (disable offloads, iptables clamp, validate with grpc-client and iperf). Linking results here after validation.

ryan: follow-up items:
- make CNI MTU a cluster config parameter and validate on new node provisioning.
- add agent to detect inconsistent host vs overlay MTU and alert early.
- evaluate enabling TCP_MTU_PROBING cluster-wide temporarily.

alex: thanks all. tagging @ops for scheduling and @dena/@sanjay for postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
